articles.title: Psychology says going silent on a text isn’t proof someone doesn’t care—people who stop replying tend to feel worse than you realize
articles.summary: When a casual text goes unanswered, it’s easy to assume you were annoying and the other person simply doesn’t care. Psychology research suggests people who go silent often feel worse than waiting friends expect—and sending even a brief reply cuts self-blame and narrows the gap.

articles.title: Violent video games do not drive real-world crime, national data shows
articles.summary: A new analysis of national crime statistics indicates that violent video games do not drive spikes in real-world violence. Researchers actually observed occasional drops in homicides and aggravated assaults during periods of high video game consumption.

articles.title: Flipping the genders in classic opinion polls uncovers a wide gap in perceived gender neutrality
articles.summary: On standard polls about women, Americans describe society as relatively progressive. Flip those statements to ask about men, however, and half expect different social judgments, a gap that helps predict spousal income differences.

articles.title: People who have four or more caffeinated drinks a day don’t rate their sleep any worse — and neuroscience found a surprising fact about their sleep
articles.summary: Drinking four or more caffeinated beverages a day might sound like a recipe for poor sleep, yet new neuroscience research suggests the body adapts in a surprising way. Heavy daily drinkers got only about 11 to 13 minutes less sleep without rating their rest any worse—and their brain waves showed they actually slept more deeply.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? articles.title: Scientists at Meta decode typed sentences from brain activity without surgically implanted chips
articles.summary: Brain implants can translate neural activity into text, but they require risky neurosurgery. A new Nature Neuroscience study shows magnetic brain scans and AI can reconstruct typed sentences from outside the skull.

articles.title: Dark personality traits spark moral disgust even when nobody gets hurt
articles.summary: Moral anger and disgust often overlap, but new experiments suggest they track different cues. While harmful outcomes fuel anger and confrontation, harmless displays of dark personality traits spark disgust and social avoidance.

articles.title: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.31301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces. We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. Fakes cover inner-face swapping, whole-frame video diffusion and voice conversion. MOZAIC has 137,745 clips from 1
